source.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לָמ֑וּת וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵ֠לָיו יְשַׁעְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־אָמ֜וֹץ הַנָּבִ֗יא וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ צַ֣ו לְבֵיתֶ֔ךָ כִּ֛י מֵ֥ת אַתָּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִֽחְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In the days those became sick Hezekiah to die, and came to him Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet and said to him, thus says Yahweh: command to your household, for dying you [are] and not you will live.

en.L: In those days Hezekiah became sick to [the point of] dying, and Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, came to him and said to him, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Give command to your household, for you are dying, and you will not live."
en.B: In those days Hezekiah fell ill and was close to death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Give final instructions to your household, for you are dying and will not live."
en.R: Around that time Hezekiah became so sick that he was about to die. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to see him. He said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Tell your family what they must do after you are gone. You are going to die. You will not get well."

es.L: En aquellos días Ezequías enfermó de muerte, y vino a él el profeta Isaías hijo de Amoz y le dijo: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Da órdenes a tu casa, porque vas a morir y no vivirás».
es.B: En aquellos días Ezequías cayó enfermo y estuvo a punto de morir. El profeta Isaías hijo de Amoz fue a verlo y le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Da tus últimas instrucciones a tu familia, porque vas a morir; no vivirás».
es.R: Por aquel tiempo Ezequías se enfermó tanto que estaba a punto de morir. El profeta Isaías hijo de Amoz fue a verlo. Le dijo: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Dile a tu familia lo que deben hacer cuando ya no estés. Vas a morir. No te vas a sanar».

fr.L: En ces jours-là, Ézéchias fut malade à en mourir, et Isaïe fils d’Amots, le prophète, vint auprès de lui et lui dit : « Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Donne tes ordres à ta maison, car tu vas mourir, et tu ne vivras pas. »
fr.B: En ce temps-là, Ézéchias tomba malade et fut sur le point de mourir. Le prophète Isaïe, fils d’Amots, vint le voir et lui dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Donne tes dernières instructions à ta famille, car tu vas mourir ; tu ne vivras pas. »
fr.R: À cette époque, Ézéchias est tombé tellement malade qu’il allait mourir. Le prophète Isaïe fils d’Amots est venu le voir. Il lui a dit : « Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Dis à ta famille ce qu’elle devra faire après ta mort. Tu vas mourir. Tu ne guériras pas. »

sw.L: Katika siku hizo Hezekia aliugua [karibu] kufa, naye Isaya mwana wa Amozi, nabii, akaja kwake, akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Toa maagizo kwa watu wa nyumba yako, kwa maana unakufa, wala hutaishi."
sw.B: Siku hizo Hezekia aliugua, akakaribia kufa. Nabii Isaya mwana wa Amozi akaja kwake, akamwambia, "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Toa maagizo yako ya mwisho kwa watu wa nyumba yako, kwa maana unakufa, wala hutapona."
sw.R: Wakati huo Hezekia aliugua sana hata akakaribia kufa. Nabii Isaya mwana wa Amozi akaja kumwona. Akasema, "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Waambie watu wa familia yako yale watakayopaswa kufanya baada ya wewe kuondoka. Utakufa. Hutapona."

vi.L: Trong những ngày ấy, Ê-xê-chia lâm bệnh gần chết. Nhà tiên tri Ê-sai con trai A-mốt đến gặp vua và nói với vua: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Hãy truyền lệnh cho nhà vua, vì vua sắp chết, không sống được nữa."
vi.B: Trong những ngày ấy, Ê-xê-chia lâm bệnh nặng gần chết. Nhà tiên tri Ê-sai con trai A-mốt đến gặp vua và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Hãy dặn dò người nhà lần cuối, vì vua sắp chết, không sống được nữa."
vi.R: Khoảng thời gian ấy, Ê-xê-chia bệnh nặng đến nỗi sắp chết. Nhà tiên tri Ê-sai con trai A-mốt đến thăm vua. Ông nói: "Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Hãy dặn gia đình vua những việc họ phải làm sau khi vua qua đời. Vua sắp chết rồi. Vua sẽ không khỏi bệnh."

ko.L: 그 날들에 히스기야가 병들어 죽게 되었다. 그러자 아모스의 아들 예언자 이사야가 그에게 와서 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하십니다. '네 집안에 명령을 내려라. 네가 죽고 살지 못할 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그 무렵 히스기야가 병이 들어 죽게 되었다. 아모스의 아들 예언자 이사야가 그에게 와서 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하십니다. '네 집안일을 정리하여라. 네가 죽을 것이고 살지 못할 것이다.'"
ko.R: 그 무렵 히스기야가 병이 들어 거의 죽게 되었다. 아모스의 아들 예언자 이사야가 그를 찾아와서 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀입니다. '네가 죽은 뒤에 네 가족이 할 일을 일러 두어라. 너는 죽을 것이다. 병이 낫지 않을 것이다.'"

decisions.choice: in those days: during the years of Sennacherib's threat to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The phrase ties the illness loosely to the events of chapters 18-19. Verse 6 still promises rescue from the king of Assyria, so the illness came before that danger had ended. 2 Chronicles 32:24 tells the same event briefly.

decisions.choice: give command to your household: settle your affairs and give your last instructions before death
decisions.reason: The same words are said to Ahithophel before he dies (2 Samuel 17:23). A dying man told his family how his goods and duties were to be handled.

decisions.choice: you are dying, and you will not live: death is near and the illness will not be cured
decisions.reason: The participle describes death as already on its way. The second clause says the same thing again from the other side: Hezekiah will not recover. Verse 5 shows that the sentence could still be turned back in answer to prayer.

decisions.choice: the same account as Isaiah 38:1-8 and 39:1-8
decisions.reason: Verses 1-19 of this chapter tell the same story as Isaiah 38-39, often in the same words. This verse is word for word the same as Isaiah 38:1, and is rendered the same way. Where the two accounts differ, a note on that verse says how. The poem Hezekiah wrote after his recovery (Isaiah 38:9-20) has no parallel in Kings.

decisions.choice: Tell your family what they must do after you are gone
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what the idiom means (m2), as at Isaiah 38:1.

decisions.choice: "Da órdenes a tu casa" (L); "Da tus últimas instrucciones a tu familia" (B); "Dile a tu familia lo que deben hacer cuando ya no estés" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew wording; Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m2), as the English does.

decisions.choice: Isaiah to Hezekiah: vua
decisions.reason: A prophet calls the king "vua", as the terms note sets; the message is from the LORD but Isaiah relays it in his own respectful voice, so the king is not "ngươi" here.

ko.R: 히스기야는 몸을 돌려 벽을 향하고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도했다.

decisions.choice: turned his face to the wall: turned away from the people in the room to pray alone
decisions.reason: Lying on his sickbed, the king turns away from those around him. The act shows that his prayer is private and earnest, not that he turns from God (compare 1 Kings 21:4, where Ahab turns his face away in sulking).

decisions.choice: the same as Isaiah 38:2, without the name and with "saying"
decisions.reason: Isaiah 38:2 names Hezekiah as the one who turned. Kings says only "he" and ends with "saying", which leads straight into the prayer; Isaiah begins the prayer with "and he said" instead (Isaiah 38:3).

decisions.choice: Hezekiah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the king, who is the subject from verse 1, as Isaiah 38:2 does.

source.text: אָנָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה זְכָר־נָ֞א אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לְפָנֶ֗יךָ בֶּֽאֱמֶת֙ וּבְלֵבָ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם וְהַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עָשִׂ֑יתִי וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכִ֥י גָדֽוֹל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Please, Yahweh, remember please how I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a heart whole, and the good in your eyes I have done. And wept Hezekiah weeping great.

en.L: "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember, please, how I have walked before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and [that] I have done what [is] good in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes." And Hezekiah wept [with] great weeping.
en.B: "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember how I have lived before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} faithfully and with an undivided heart, doing what is good in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight." And Hezekiah wept loudly.
en.R: "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please remember how I have always been faithful to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I have served {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all my heart. I have done what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see as good." Then Hezekiah cried very hard.

es.L: «Te ruego, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, acuérdate, te ruego, de cómo he andado delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} con fidelidad y con corazón íntegro, y he hecho lo bueno ante {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos». Y lloró Ezequías con gran llanto.
es.B: «Te ruego, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que recuerdes cómo he vivido delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} con fidelidad y con un corazón entero, haciendo lo que es bueno a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} ojos». Y Ezequías lloró amargamente.
es.R: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, por favor, recuerda que siempre te he sido fiel. Te he servido con todo mi corazón. He hecho lo que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} consideras bueno». Luego Ezequías lloró desconsoladamente.

fr.L: « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} donc que j’ai marché devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} avec fidélité et d’un cœur entier, et que j’ai fait ce qui [est] bien à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} yeux. » Et Ézéchias pleura abondamment.
fr.B: « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que j’ai vécu devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} avec fidélité et d’un cœur sans partage, et que j’ai fait ce qui est bien à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} yeux. » Et Ézéchias pleura à chaudes larmes.
fr.R: « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai toujours été fidèle. Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai servi de tout mon cœur. J’ai fait ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} trouves bien. » Puis Ézéchias a beaucoup pleuré.

sw.L: "Tafadhali, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kumbuka, tafadhali, jinsi nilivyoenenda mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kwa uaminifu na kwa moyo mkamilifu, na [kwamba] nimefanya yaliyo mema machoni {{deity_pronoun:pako|Pako}}." Naye Hezekia akalia kilio kikuu.
sw.B: "Tafadhali, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kumbuka jinsi nilivyoishi mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kwa uaminifu na kwa moyo usiogawanyika, nikifanya yaliyo mema machoni {{deity_pronoun:pako|Pako}}." Naye Hezekia akalia kwa sauti kubwa.
sw.R: "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali kumbuka jinsi ambavyo nimekuwa mwaminifu kwako siku zote. Nimekutumikia kwa moyo wangu wote. Nimefanya yale unayoyaona kuwa mema." Kisha Hezekia akalia sana.

vi.L: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin Ngài nhớ lại con đã bước đi trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong sự trung tín và với một tấm lòng trọn vẹn, và đã làm điều tốt lành trước mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}." Rồi Ê-xê-chia khóc lớn.
vi.B: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhớ lại con đã sống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cách trung tín, với một lòng không chia hai, và đã làm điều tốt lành trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}." Rồi Ê-xê-chia khóc lớn.
vi.R: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhớ lại con đã luôn trung thành với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Con đã hết lòng phục vụ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Con đã làm điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy là tốt." Rồi Ê-xê-chia khóc nức nở.

ko.L: "아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 주님 앞에서 진실하게, 온전한 마음으로 걸었고, 주님의 눈에 좋은 일을 한 것을 부디 기억해 주십시오." 그리고 히스기야가 크게 울며 울었다.
ko.B: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 주님 앞에서 진실하게, 한결같은 마음으로 살아왔고, 주님 보시기에 선한 일을 해 온 것을 부디 기억해 주십시오." 그리고 히스기야는 큰 소리로 울었다.
ko.R: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 늘 주님께 충성해 온 것을 부디 기억해 주십시오. 저는 온 마음으로 주님을 섬겼습니다. 저는 주님께서 좋게 보시는 일을 했습니다." 그러고 나서 히스기야는 몹시 울었다.

decisions.choice: walked before you: lived my whole life in your presence and service
decisions.reason: To walk before God is to live in his sight and serve him (Genesis 17:1; 1 Kings 2:4). Hezekiah does not claim to be sinless (Isaiah 38:17 speaks of his sins); he appeals to a life of loyalty, the life described in 18:3-6.

decisions.choice: in faithfulness and with a whole heart: with steady loyalty and undivided devotion
decisions.reason: A whole (complete) heart is one not split between God and other loyalties (1 Kings 8:61; 11:4). The word for faithfulness comes back in verse 19, where it is paired with peace.

decisions.choice: word for word the same prayer as Isaiah 38:3
decisions.reason: The prayer and the note of Hezekiah's weeping are the same as in Isaiah 38:3, and are rendered the same way. Only the opening differs: Isaiah begins "And he said", where Kings has "saying" at the end of verse 2.

decisions.choice: I have always been faithful to you. I have served you with all my heart.
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the prayer into short sentences and explains the idiom of walking before God (m1), as at Isaiah 38:3.

decisions.choice: "siempre te he sido fiel. Te he servido con todo mi corazón"
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the prayer into short sentences and gives the sense of walking before God (m1), as the English does; the pronoun "te" after the verb stays plain.

decisions.choice: deity pronoun spans on "yako", "pako"
decisions.reason: God addressed in prayer: the free possessives "mbele yako", "machoni pako" take the deity pronoun span; at Readable "kwako" after "mwaminifu" is left plain because the English Readable's spans fall on words Swahili marks in the verb.

decisions.choice: the middle court: the reading given in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell "the city", which gives "the middle city", an odd phrase for a place inside Jerusalem. The Hebrew margin tells the reader to read "court" instead, and the ancient Greek translation also has "the middle court". The margin's reading is followed. On either reading Isaiah had hardly left the palace grounds.

decisions.choice: the middle court: one of the courtyards of the royal buildings
decisions.reason: The king's palace stood next to the temple, with courtyards around and between the buildings (1 Kings 7:1-12). Isaiah had just left Hezekiah's sickroom and was still crossing one of these courts when the new word came. The answer to the prayer came at once.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 38:4 does not say where Isaiah was
decisions.reason: Isaiah 38:4 has only "And the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying". Kings adds that Isaiah had not yet gone out of the middle court, and says the word came "to him".

decisions.choice: yet
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says he "had not gone out"; "yet" makes clear that he was still on his way out. Literal brackets it. Readable says the same with "before ... even".

records.literal_gloss: Turn back and you will say to Hezekiah [the] ruler of my people, thus says Yahweh the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears; here I [am] healing you; on the day the third you will go up [to the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: "Go back and say to Hezekiah, the ruler of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look, I am healing you. On the third day you will go up [to the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: "Go back and say to Hezekiah, the ruler of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestor David, says this: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. I am about to heal you, and on the third day you will go up to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: "Go back and tell Hezekiah, the leader of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says, the God your ancestor David served: I have heard your prayer, and I have seen you crying. So I will heal you. On the third day you will be well enough to go up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house.

es.L: «Vuelve y di a Ezequías, gobernante de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de David tu padre: He oído tu oración; he visto tus lágrimas. He aquí que yo te sano. Al tercer día subirás [a la] casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: «Regresa y dile a Ezequías, gobernante de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de tu antepasado David, dice esto: He oído tu oración; he visto tus lágrimas. Voy a sanarte, y al tercer día subirás a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: «Regresa y dile a Ezequías, el líder de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios a quien sirvió tu antepasado David: He oído tu oración y he visto tus lágrimas. Por eso te voy a sanar. Al tercer día estarás tan bien que podrás subir a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

Voici, je te guéris. Le troisième jour, tu monteras [à] la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: « Retourne dire à Ézéchias, le chef de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de ton ancêtre David, dit ceci : J’ai entendu ta prière, j’ai vu tes larmes. Je vais te guérir, et le troisième jour tu monteras à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: « Retourne dire à Ézéchias, le chef de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple : “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu que ton ancêtre David a servi : J’ai entendu ta prière et je t’ai vu pleurer. Alors je vais te guérir. Le troisième jour, tu seras assez bien pour monter au temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.B: "Rudi ukamwambie Hezekia, kiongozi wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa babu yako Daudi, asema hivi: Nimeyasikia maombi yako; nimeyaona machozi yako. Nitakuponya, na siku ya tatu utapanda kwenda nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: "Hãy quay lại và nói với Ê-xê-chia, người lãnh đạo dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Đa-vít tổ phụ ngươi, phán thế này: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nghe lời cầu nguyện của ngươi; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy nước mắt ngươi. Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chữa lành ngươi. Ngày thứ ba ngươi sẽ đi lên nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: "Hãy quay lại nói với Ê-xê-chia, người lãnh đạo dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Đa-vít tổ tiên con, phán như vầy: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nghe lời con cầu nguyện; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy nước mắt con. Ta sắp chữa lành con, và đến ngày thứ ba con sẽ đi lên nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: "Hãy quay lại nói với Ê-xê-chia, người lãnh đạo dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: 'Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời mà Đa-vít tổ tiên con đã phục vụ, phán: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nghe lời con cầu nguyện, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy con khóc. Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ chữa lành con. Đến ngày thứ ba con sẽ khỏe đủ để đi lên đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: "돌아가서 내 백성의 지도자 히스기야에게 말하여라. '네 조상 다윗의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 이와 같이 말한다. 내가 네 기도를 들었고 네 눈물을 보았다. 보아라, 내가 너를 고치겠다. 셋째 날에 네가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집으로 올라갈 것이다.
ko.B: "돌아가서 내 백성의 지도자 히스기야에게 말하여라. '네 조상 다윗의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 이렇게 말한다. 내가 네 기도를 들었고 네 눈물을 보았다. 내가 너를 고쳐 주겠다. 사흘째 되는 날에 너는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집으로 올라갈 것이다.
ko.R: "돌아가서 내 백성의 지도자 히스기야에게 전하여라. '네 조상 다윗이 섬긴 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 하는 말이다. 내가 네 기도를 들었고, 네가 우는 것을 보았다. 그러니 내가 너를 고쳐 주겠다. 사흘째 되는 날에 너는 나아서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전에 올라갈 수 있을 것이다.

decisions.choice: the ruler of my people: the one God has set over his people
decisions.reason: The title is the one given to Saul and David when God chose them (1 Samuel 9:16; 2 Samuel 7:8). It reminds Hezekiah that he holds the kingdom from God and rules God's people, not his own.

decisions.choice: David your father: David your ancestor
decisions.reason: David lived about three hundred years before Hezekiah. Calling God the God of David reminds Hezekiah of the promise made to David's line (2 Samuel 7:16), which verse 6 goes on to name.

decisions.choice: here I am healing you: the healing is as good as done
decisions.reason: The particle with a participle announces what God is about to do. The same verb comes back in Hezekiah's question in verse 8.

decisions.choice: on the third day you will go up to the house of the LORD: in two days he would be well enough to worship at the temple
decisions.reason: Days were counted with the present day as the first, so the third day is the day after tomorrow. To go up to the temple was to appear in public again and give thanks there (compare Isaiah 38:20). The promise names a near and checkable day, which is why Hezekiah asks for a sign in verse 8.

decisions.choice: differs from Isaiah 38:5 in three places
decisions.reason: Isaiah 38:5 has "Go" where Kings has "Go back", does not have "the ruler of my people", and does not have "I am healing you; on the third day you will go up to the house of the LORD". In Isaiah 38:5 the speech goes straight on to the fifteen years. Isaiah keeps only Hezekiah's question about going up to the house of the LORD (Isaiah 38:22).

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: Readable says "leader" for the title "ruler", as throughout these books.

decisions.choice: you will be well enough to go up
decisions.reason: Readable says why going up to the temple matters: it would mean he was healed (m4).

decisions.choice: "gobernante" (L, B); "líder" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for nagid: "gobernante" at Literal and Balanced, "líder" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "le chef de mon peuple"
decisions.reason: *Nagid* is "chef" at every level, as the Samuel terms note sets.

decisions.choice: God names himself without the honorific ("하나님 주가 이와 같이 말한다")
decisions.reason: Here God himself dictates the message Isaiah is to give, so the self-reference has no -시-; where Isaiah reports God's word (verse 1) the honorific stays.

records.literal_gloss: And I will add to your days fifteen year[s], and from [the] palm of [the] king of Assyria I will deliver you and the city this, and I will defend over the city this for my sake and for the sake of David my servant.

en.L: And I will add fifteen years to your days, and from the hand of the king of Assyria I will deliver you and this city, and I will defend this city for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake and for the sake of David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave.'"
en.B: I will add fifteen years to your days. I will rescue you and this city from the grasp of the king of Assyria, and I will shield this city for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own sake and for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David's sake.'"
en.R: I will let you live fifteen more years. I will save you and this city from the power of the king of Assyria. I will protect this city for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own honor, and because of the promise I made to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David.'"

es.L: Y añadiré a tus días quince años, y de la palma del rey de Asiria te libraré a ti y a esta ciudad, y ampararé esta ciudad por amor de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo y por amor de David {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo”».
es.B: Añadiré quince años a tu vida. Te libraré a ti y a esta ciudad de las garras del rey de Asiria, y protegeré esta ciudad por amor a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo y por amor a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David”».
es.R: Te dejaré vivir quince años más. Los salvaré a ti y a esta ciudad del poder del rey de Asiria. Protegeré esta ciudad por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} propia honra, y por la promesa que le hice a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David”».

fr.L: Et j’ajouterai à tes jours quinze ans, et de la main du roi d’Assyrie je te délivrerai, toi et cette ville, et je protégerai cette ville à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et à cause de David {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esclave.” »
fr.B: J’ajouterai quinze années à tes jours. Je te délivrerai, toi et cette ville, de la main du roi d’Assyrie, et je protégerai cette ville à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et à cause de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur David.” »
fr.R: Je vais te laisser vivre encore quinze ans. Je vous sauverai, toi et cette ville, du pouvoir du roi d’Assyrie. Je protégerai cette ville pour {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} honneur, et à cause de la promesse que j’ai faite à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur David.” »

sw.L: Nami nitaziongeza siku zako miaka kumi na mitano, na kutoka mkononi mwa mfalme wa Ashuru nitakuokoa wewe na mji huu, nami nitaulinda mji huu kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kwa ajili ya Daudi mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.'"
sw.B: Nitakuongezea miaka kumi na mitano ya kuishi. Nitakuokoa wewe na mji huu kutoka katika makucha ya mfalme wa Ashuru, nami nitaukinga mji huu kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mwenyewe na kwa ajili ya mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Daudi.'"
sw.R: Nitakuacha uishi miaka kumi na mitano zaidi. Nitakuokoa wewe na mji huu kutoka katika mamlaka ya mfalme wa Ashuru. Nitaulinda mji huu kwa ajili ya heshima {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mwenyewe, na kwa sababu ya ahadi niliyompa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Daudi.'"

vi.L: Ta sẽ thêm cho ngươi mười lăm năm, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giải cứu ngươi và thành này khỏi tay vua A-si-ri, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ che chở thành này vì cớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vì cớ Đa-vít đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'"
vi.B: Ta sẽ thêm tuổi thọ cho con mười lăm năm. Ta sẽ giải cứu con và thành này khỏi tay vua A-si-ri, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ che chở thành này vì cớ chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vì cớ Đa-vít đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'"
vi.R: Ta sẽ cho con sống thêm mười lăm năm nữa. Ta sẽ cứu con và thành này khỏi quyền lực của vua A-si-ri. Ta sẽ bảo vệ thành này vì danh dự của chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và vì lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã hứa với Đa-vít đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'"

ko.L: 그리고 내가 네 날들에 십오 년을 더하겠고, 너와 이 성을 앗시리아 왕의 손바닥에서 건져 내겠다. 그리고 내가 나를 위하여, 내 종 다윗을 위하여 이 성을 보호하겠다.'"
ko.B: 내가 네 수명을 십오 년 더 늘려 주겠다. 너와 이 성을 앗시리아 왕의 손아귀에서 건져 내겠다. 나 자신을 위하여, 그리고 내 종 다윗을 위하여 내가 이 성을 지키겠다.'"
ko.R: 내가 너를 십오 년 더 살게 하겠다. 내가 너와 이 성을 앗시리아 왕의 손에서 구해 내겠다. 내 이름의 영광을 위하여, 그리고 내 종 다윗에게 한 약속 때문에 내가 이 성을 지키겠다.'"

decisions.choice: I will add fifteen years: a promise of a set span of life
decisions.reason: The fifteen years fit the history: Hezekiah's illness came about 701 BC, and his reign ended about 686 BC. His son Manasseh was twelve when he became king (21:1), so he was born in these added years.

decisions.choice: from the palm of the king: from his power and control
decisions.reason: Hand or palm stands for the power to hold and harm (18:29-35).

decisions.choice: I will defend this city for my sake and for David's: the promise already given in 19:34
decisions.reason: God made the same promise, in the same words, in 19:34 (Isaiah 37:35). Isaiah 38:6 repeats only "I will defend this city"; Kings repeats the whole promise. Isaiah 38:5 also says "Look, I am adding" where Kings says "And I will add"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: for my sake and for the sake of David: God acts for his own name and his promise to David
decisions.reason: The Assyrian king had mocked the LORD as one more god who could not save (18:33-35; 19:10-13). God defends the city to show who he is, and to keep his promise that David's line would rule in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 7:16; 1 Kings 11:13).

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: Literal says "slave" in "my servant David", as throughout these books; Balanced and Readable say "servant". Isaiah 38:6 does not have these words. At 19:34 every level keeps "servant", because that verse repeats Isaiah 37:35.

decisions.choice: for my own honor, and because of the promise I made to my servant David
decisions.reason: Readable says what acting for God's own sake and for David's sake means (m4), as at Isaiah 37:35.

decisions.choice: "mi siervo"
decisions.reason: God's "my servant David" is "siervo" at every level, Literal included, as the Samuel terms note sets for all five languages.

decisions.choice: "esclave" (L)
decisions.reason: As the English Literal here, *ʿeved* is "esclave" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "serviteur" ("my servant David" in 19:34 keeps "serviteur" at every level, as the Samuel note sets for God's own words).

records.literal_gloss: And said Isaiah, take a cake of figs. And they took and they put [it] on the boil, and he lived.

en.L: And Isaiah said, "Take a cake of figs." And they took [it] and laid [it] on the boil, and he lived.
en.B: Then Isaiah said, "Bring a lump of pressed figs." They brought it and spread it on the sore, and he recovered.
en.R: Then Isaiah said, "Bring some pressed figs." They brought them and put them on Hezekiah's sore, and he got well.

es.L: E Isaías dijo: «{{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} una masa de higos». Y [la] tomaron y [la] pusieron sobre la llaga, y sanó.
es.B: Entonces Isaías dijo: «{{plural_you:Traigan|Traed}} una masa de higos prensados». La trajeron y la aplicaron sobre la llaga, y el rey se recuperó.
es.R: Entonces Isaías dijo: «{{plural_you:Traigan|Traed}} unos higos prensados». Los trajeron y los pusieron sobre la llaga de Ezequías, y él se sanó.

fr.L: Et Isaïe dit : « Prenez un gâteau de figues. » Et ils [le] prirent et [l’]appliquèrent sur l’ulcère, et il vécut.
fr.B: Puis Isaïe dit : « Apportez une masse de figues pressées. » On l’apporta, on l’appliqua sur l’ulcère, et le roi se rétablit.
fr.R: Ensuite Isaïe a dit : « Apportez des figues écrasées. » On les a apportées et on les a mises sur l’abcès d’Ézéchias, et il a guéri.

sw.L: Naye Isaya akasema, "Chukueni andazi la tini." Nao wakalichukua, wakaliweka juu ya jipu, naye akaishi.
sw.B: Kisha Isaya akasema, "Leteni donge la tini zilizoshindiliwa." Wakalileta, wakalipaka juu ya jipu, naye akapona.
sw.R: Kisha Isaya akasema, "Leteni tini zilizoshindiliwa." Wakazileta, wakaziweka juu ya jipu la Hezekia, naye akapona.

vi.L: Ê-sai nói: "Hãy lấy một bánh trái vả." Họ lấy [nó] và đắp [nó] trên mụn nhọt, và vua sống.
vi.B: Rồi Ê-sai nói: "Hãy đem một bánh trái vả ép đến." Họ đem đến và đắp lên chỗ ung nhọt, và vua được bình phục.
vi.R: Rồi Ê-sai nói: "Hãy đem ít trái vả ép đến." Họ đem đến và đắp lên chỗ ung nhọt của Ê-xê-chia, và vua được lành bệnh.

ko.L: 그리고 이사야가 말했다. "무화과 뭉치를 가져오너라." 그러자 그들이 [그것을] 가져다가 종기 위에 붙였고, 그가 살아났다.
ko.B: 이사야가 말했다. "무화과 반죽 한 덩이를 가져오너라." 사람들이 그것을 가져다가 종기에 붙이자 왕이 회복되었다.
ko.R: 이사야가 말했다. "무화과를 눌러 만든 덩이를 가져오너라." 사람들이 그것을 가져다가 히스기야의 종기에 붙였다. 그러자 그가 나았다.

decisions.choice: a cake of figs on the boil: a common remedy
decisions.reason: Pressed figs were made into cakes for food (1 Samuel 25:18) and were also used to dress sores. The illness is named as a boil or inflamed sore, the word used of the boils in Exodus 9:9. God gives the healing; the figs are the means.

decisions.choice: the figs are applied here; Isaiah 38:21 places the order at the end
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 38:21 the order comes after Hezekiah's poem, as a look back: "let them take a cake of figs and rub it on the boil, and he will live". Kings tells it here, in the flow of the story, and says it was done: they took the figs and laid them on the boil, and he lived.

decisions.choice: and he lived: he recovered, the outcome told ahead of the sign
decisions.reason: Verse 7 ends the healing story with its outcome. Verse 8 then goes back to Hezekiah's question, asked before the third day came, and verses 9-11 tell the sign. The order is by topic, not strictly by time.

decisions.choice: Hezekiah's sore
decisions.reason: Readable names whose sore it was.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}}
decisions.reason: Isaiah speaks to the king's servants as a group, so the command carries the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: andazi la tini (Literal); donge la tini zilizoshindiliwa (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Dried figs pressed into a cake, a common remedy (meaning decision m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ אֶֽל־יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ מָ֣ה א֔וֹת כִּֽי־יִרְפָּ֥א יְהוָ֖ה לִ֑י וְעָלִ֛יתִי בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖י בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Hezekiah to Isaiah, what [is the] sign that will heal Yahweh me, and I will go up on the day the third [to the] house of Yahweh?

en.L: And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What [is the] sign that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will heal me, and [that] I will go up on the third day [to the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"
en.B: Hezekiah had asked Isaiah, "What sign will there be that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to heal me, and that on the third day I will go up to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"
en.R: Hezekiah had asked Isaiah, "What sign will show me that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will heal me? How will I know that I will go up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house on the third day?"

es.L: Y Ezequías dijo a Isaías: «¿Cuál [es la] señal de que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me sanará, y [de que] subiré al tercer día [a la] casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?».
es.B: Ezequías le había preguntado a Isaías: «¿Qué señal habrá de que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me va a sanar y de que al tercer día subiré a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?».
es.R: Ezequías le había preguntado a Isaías: «¿Qué señal me mostrará que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me va a sanar? ¿Cómo sabré que al tercer día subiré a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?».

fr.L: Et Ézéchias dit à Isaïe : « Quel [est le] signe que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me guérira, et que je monterai le troisième jour [à] la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? »
fr.B: Ézéchias avait demandé à Isaïe : « À quel signe saurai-je que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va me guérir et que, le troisième jour, je monterai à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? »
fr.R: Ézéchias avait demandé à Isaïe : « Quel signe me montrera que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va me guérir ? Comment saurai-je que je monterai au temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} le troisième jour ? »

sw.L: Naye Hezekia akamwambia Isaya, "Ni ishara gani kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataniponya, na [kwamba] nitapanda siku ya tatu [kwenda] nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?"
sw.B: Hezekia alikuwa amemwuliza Isaya, "Kutakuwa na ishara gani kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataniponya, na kwamba siku ya tatu nitapanda kwenda nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?"
sw.R: Hezekia alikuwa amemwuliza Isaya, "Ni ishara gani itakayonionyesha kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataniponya? Nitajuaje kwamba siku ya tatu nitapanda kwenda nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?"

vi.L: Ê-xê-chia nói với Ê-sai: "Dấu hiệu nào cho biết {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ chữa lành ta, và [rằng] ngày thứ ba ta sẽ đi lên nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}?"
vi.B: Ê-xê-chia đã hỏi Ê-sai: "Có dấu hiệu nào cho biết {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ chữa lành ta, và đến ngày thứ ba ta sẽ đi lên nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không?"
vi.R: Ê-xê-chia đã hỏi Ê-sai: "Dấu hiệu nào cho ta biết {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ chữa lành ta? Làm sao ta biết ngày thứ ba ta sẽ đi lên đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}?"

ko.L: 그리고 히스기야가 이사야에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 고치시고, 내가 셋째 날에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집으로 올라가게 될 표징이 무엇이오?"
ko.B: 히스기야가 이사야에게 물었었다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 고쳐 주시고 내가 사흘째 되는 날에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에 올라가게 된다는 표징이 무엇이오?"
ko.R: 히스기야가 이사야에게 물었었다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 고쳐 주실 것을 무엇으로 알 수 있겠소? 내가 사흘째 되는 날에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전에 올라가게 된다는 것을 어떻게 알겠소?"

decisions.choice: the sign: a visible event that guarantees the promise
decisions.reason: A sign is something God does that can be seen, given to confirm a word that has not yet come true (19:29; Isaiah 7:11, 14). Hezekiah asks for one; his father Ahaz had refused the sign God offered him (Isaiah 7:10-12).

decisions.choice: Hezekiah asked: the question came before the healing described in verse 7
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual one for the next step in a story, but the question belongs before the third day, when the healing was still to come (see verse 7, m3). The question looks back to the promise of verse 5.

decisions.choice: a fuller form of the question in Isaiah 38:22
decisions.reason: Isaiah 38:22 asks only "What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?" and puts the question at the end of the chapter. Kings adds "that the LORD will heal me" and "on the third day", and puts the question before the sign is given.

decisions.choice: had asked
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "had asked" so the question does not seem to come after the recovery told in verse 7 (m2), as Isaiah 38:22 does.

decisions.choice: two questions
decisions.reason: Readable splits the one Hebrew question into two shorter ones.

decisions.choice: "le había preguntado"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the pluperfect so the question does not seem to come after the recovery told in verse 7, as the English does.

decisions.choice: plus-que-parfait "avait demandé" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The question came before the healing told in verse 7 (m2); French shows it with the pluperfect, as the English "had asked" does.

decisions.choice: the king to Isaiah: ta / ông
decisions.reason: The king says "ta" for himself and "ông" to the prophet, as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: Hezekiah speaks to Isaiah in 하오체 ("무엇이오?")
decisions.reason: As David speaks to Nathan and Gad in the Samuel drafts: a king to a prophet he honors, neither down to a subject nor up to a superior.

decisions.choice: "물었었다"
decisions.reason: As the English "had asked": the question came before the healing told in verse 7.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֗הוּ זֶה־לְּךָ֤ הָאוֹת֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֚י יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר הָלַ֤ךְ הַצֵּל֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר מַֽעֲל֔וֹת אִם־יָשׁ֖וּב עֶ֥שֶׂר מַעֲלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Isaiah, this [is] for you the sign from Yahweh, that will do Yahweh the thing which he has spoken: has gone the shadow ten steps, or will it go back ten steps?

en.L: And Isaiah said, "This [is] the sign for you from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do the thing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken: [shall] the shadow go forward ten steps, or shall it go back ten steps?"
en.B: Isaiah answered, "This will be your sign from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will carry out what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said: Should the shadow go forward ten steps, or should it go back ten steps?"
en.R: Isaiah answered, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will give you a sign to show that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised. You choose: Should the shadow move ahead ten steps, or should it go back ten steps?"

es.L: E Isaías dijo: «Esta [es] para ti la señal de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, de que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hará lo que ha dicho: ¿[Avanzará] la sombra diez peldaños, o retrocederá diez peldaños?».
es.B: Isaías respondió: «Esta será tu señal de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} cumplirá lo que ha dicho: ¿Quieres que la sombra avance diez peldaños, o que retroceda diez peldaños?».
es.R: Isaías le contestó: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te dará una señal para mostrarte que hará lo que ha prometido. Tú eliges: ¿Debe la sombra avanzar diez peldaños, o debe retroceder diez peldaños?».

fr.L: Et Isaïe dit : « Voici pour toi le signe de la part {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} accomplira la parole qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dite : l’ombre avancera-t-elle de dix degrés, ou reculera-t-elle de dix degrés ? »
fr.B: Isaïe répondit : « Voici le signe que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te donne pour montrer qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} accomplira ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : l’ombre doit-elle avancer de dix marches, ou reculer de dix marches ? »
fr.R: Isaïe a répondu : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va te donner un signe pour montrer qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fera ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis. À toi de choisir : l’ombre doit-elle avancer de dix marches, ou reculer de dix marches ? »

sw.L: Naye Isaya akasema, "Hii [ndiyo] ishara kwako kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atalifanya jambo alilolinena: Je, kivuli kiende mbele hatua kumi, au kirudi nyuma hatua kumi?"
sw.B: Isaya akajibu, "Hii itakuwa ishara yako kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atalitimiza alilosema: Je, kivuli kiende mbele hatua kumi, au kirudi nyuma hatua kumi?"
sw.R: Isaya akajibu, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakupa ishara ya kuonyesha kwamba atafanya yale aliyoahidi. Wewe chagua: Je, kivuli kisogee mbele hatua kumi, au kirudi nyuma hatua kumi?"

vi.L: Ê-sai nói: "Đây [là] dấu hiệu từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho vua, rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ làm điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán: bóng [sẽ] tiến tới mười bậc, hay sẽ lùi lại mười bậc?"
vi.B: Ê-sai đáp: "Đây là dấu hiệu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho vua để biết {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ thực hiện điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán: Bóng nắng nên tiến tới mười bậc, hay nên lùi lại mười bậc?"
vi.R: Ê-sai đáp: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ ban cho vua một dấu hiệu để cho thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hứa. Xin vua chọn: Bóng nắng nên tiến tới mười bậc, hay nên lùi lại mười bậc?"

ko.L: 그리고 이사야가 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 그 일을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이루실 것이라는, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 임금님께 주시는 표징은 이것입니다. 그림자가 열 계단 앞으로 나아가야 하겠습니까, 아니면 열 계단 뒤로 물러가야 하겠습니까?"
ko.B: 이사야가 대답했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 것을 이루실 것이라는 표징으로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 임금님께 주시는 것은 이것입니다. 그림자가 열 계단 앞으로 나아가기를 원하십니까, 아니면 열 계단 뒤로 물러가기를 원하십니까?"
ko.R: 이사야가 대답했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 약속하신 일을 꼭 이루신다는 것을 보여 주시려고 임금님께 표징을 주실 것입니다. 임금님께서 고르십시오. 그림자가 열 계단 앞으로 나아가게 할까요, 아니면 열 계단 뒤로 물러가게 할까요?"

decisions.choice: shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or go back: Hezekiah is offered a choice
alternatives: The shadow has gone forward ten steps; shall it go back ten steps?
decisions.reason: The first verb is in a form that normally speaks of the past and has no question marker, so the line could be read "The shadow has gone forward ten steps; shall it go back ten steps?" But the word "or" sets two options side by side, and Hezekiah's answer in verse 10 chooses between them. The record reads the whole line as a question offering a choice.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 38:7-8 has no choice
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 38:7-8 God simply announces that the shadow will go back ten steps. In Kings Isaiah lets Hezekiah choose which way the shadow will move. The opening words are almost the same as Isaiah 38:7, which has "this thing" where Kings has "the thing".

decisions.choice: the shadow and the steps: the shadow moving on a stairway as the day passes
decisions.reason: As the sun moved across the sky, the shadow cast on a stairway crept along the steps and marked the time of day (verse 11). To go forward is to move the way it always moves; to go back is to move against the course of the day.

decisions.choice: shall; should; You choose
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "shall" to show the question that the line implies (m1). Readable adds "You choose" to make plain that Hezekiah is being offered a choice.

decisions.choice: "degrés" (L); "marches" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The shadow moved on a stairway (m3); Literal keeps the traditional "degrés", which are steps, and Balanced and Readable say "marches" so the picture is plain.

decisions.choice: alilolinena / aliyoahidi (no free pronoun)
decisions.reason: The English deity pronoun spans fall on "he", which Swahili marks in the verb prefix; no span is possible there.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ נָקֵ֣ל לַצֵּ֔ל לִנְט֖וֹת עֶ֣שֶׂר מַעֲל֑וֹת לֹ֣א כִ֔י יָשׁ֥וּב הַצֵּ֛ל אֲחֹרַנִּ֖ית עֶ֥שֶׂר מַעֲלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Hezekiah, [it is] trifling for the shadow to stretch out ten steps; no, but let go back the shadow backward ten steps.

en.L: And Hezekiah said, "It is a light thing for the shadow to stretch out ten steps. No, rather let the shadow go back backward ten steps."
en.B: Hezekiah answered, "It is easy for the shadow to lengthen ten steps. No, let the shadow go back ten steps."
en.R: Hezekiah answered, "It is easy for the shadow to move ahead ten steps, because that is what it always does. No, make the shadow go back ten steps."

es.L: Y Ezequías dijo: «Cosa fácil es que la sombra se extienda diez peldaños. No, sino que vuelva la sombra atrás diez peldaños».
es.B: Ezequías respondió: «Es fácil que la sombra se alargue diez peldaños. No, que la sombra retroceda diez peldaños».
es.R: Ezequías respondió: «Es fácil que la sombra avance diez peldaños, porque eso es lo que hace siempre. No, haz que la sombra retroceda diez peldaños».

fr.L: Et Ézéchias dit : « C’est peu de chose que l’ombre s’allonge de dix degrés. Non, mais que l’ombre recule en arrière de dix degrés. »
fr.B: Ézéchias répondit : « Il est facile pour l’ombre de s’allonger de dix marches. Non, que l’ombre recule plutôt de dix marches. »
fr.R: Ézéchias a répondu : « C’est facile pour l’ombre d’avancer de dix marches, puisque c’est ce qu’elle fait toujours. Non, fais plutôt reculer l’ombre de dix marches. »

sw.L: Naye Hezekia akasema, "Ni jambo jepesi kivuli kurefuka hatua kumi. Sivyo, bali kivuli kirudi nyuma hatua kumi."
sw.B: Hezekia akajibu, "Ni rahisi kivuli kurefuka hatua kumi. Sivyo, kivuli kirudi nyuma hatua kumi."
sw.R: Hezekia akajibu, "Ni rahisi kivuli kusogea mbele hatua kumi, kwa sababu ndivyo kinavyofanya siku zote. Sivyo, fanya kivuli kirudi nyuma hatua kumi."

vi.L: Ê-xê-chia nói: "Bóng kéo dài mười bậc là việc dễ. Không, nhưng hãy để bóng lùi lại phía sau mười bậc."
vi.B: Ê-xê-chia đáp: "Bóng nắng tiến dài thêm mười bậc thì dễ. Không, hãy để bóng lùi lại mười bậc."
vi.R: Ê-xê-chia đáp: "Bóng nắng tiến tới mười bậc thì dễ, vì nó vẫn luôn như vậy. Không, hãy làm cho bóng lùi lại mười bậc."

ko.L: 그리고 히스기야가 말했다. "그림자가 열 계단 늘어나는 것은 쉬운 일이오. 아니오, 그림자가 열 계단 뒤로 물러가게 하시오."
ko.B: 히스기야가 대답했다. "그림자가 열 계단 길어지는 것은 쉬운 일이오. 아니오, 그림자가 열 계단 뒤로 물러가게 해 주시오."
ko.R: 히스기야가 대답했다. "그림자가 열 계단 앞으로 나아가는 것은 쉬운 일이오. 그림자는 늘 그렇게 움직이니까. 아니오, 그림자가 열 계단 뒤로 물러가게 해 주시오."

decisions.choice: it is a light thing for the shadow to stretch out: going forward would be no real sign
decisions.reason: To stretch out is to lengthen, the way a shadow moves on as the day goes on. That would happen anyway, so it would prove nothing. A shadow moving back, against the course of the day, could only be God's doing.

decisions.choice: Hezekiah: here spelled in a longer form of the name
decisions.reason: Hebrew spells the king's name in more than one way. This verse uses a longer form, Yehizkiyahu, built on the verb form "he strengthens"; both forms mean "Yah strengthens". It is the same man.

decisions.choice: because that is what it always does
decisions.reason: Readable says why going forward would be easy (m1).

decisions.choice: Hezekiah
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the usual form of the name, since the longer spelling names the same king.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְשַׁעְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֶת־הַצֵּ֗ל בַּֽ֠מַּעֲלוֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרְדָ֜ה בְּמַעֲל֥וֹת אָחָ֛ז אֲחֹֽרַנִּ֖ית עֶ֥שֶׂר מַעֲלֽוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And called Isaiah the prophet to Yahweh, and he brought back the shadow on the steps which it had gone down on [the] steps of Ahaz, backward ten steps.

en.L: And Isaiah the prophet called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought the shadow back on the steps, which it had gone down on the steps of Ahaz, backward ten steps.
en.B: Then the prophet Isaiah called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the shadow go back ten steps, back up the steps of Ahaz that it had gone down.
en.R: Then the prophet Isaiah called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the shadow go back up ten of the steps it had already gone down on the stairway of Ahaz.

es.L: Y el profeta Isaías clamó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, e hizo volver la sombra por los peldaños por los que había bajado en los peldaños de Acaz, diez peldaños atrás.
es.B: Entonces el profeta Isaías clamó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo que la sombra retrocediera diez peldaños, subiendo por los peldaños de Acaz por los que había bajado.
es.R: Entonces el profeta Isaías clamó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo que la sombra subiera de nuevo diez de los peldaños que ya había bajado en la escalinata de Acaz.

fr.L: Et Isaïe le prophète cria vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fit reculer l’ombre sur les degrés qu’elle avait descendus, sur les degrés d’Achaz, de dix degrés en arrière.
fr.B: Alors le prophète Isaïe cria vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fit reculer l’ombre de dix marches, en remontant les marches d’Achaz qu’elle avait descendues.
fr.R: Alors le prophète Isaïe a prié {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} à grands cris. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait remonter l’ombre de dix des marches qu’elle avait déjà descendues sur l’escalier d’Achaz.

sw.L: Naye Isaya nabii akamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye akakirudisha kivuli katika ngazi, ambacho kilikuwa kimeshuka katika ngazi za Ahazi, nyuma hatua kumi.
sw.B: Kisha nabii Isaya akamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye akakifanya kivuli kirudi nyuma hatua kumi, kipande juu ya ngazi za Ahazi kilizokuwa kimeshuka.
sw.R: Kisha nabii Isaya akamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akakifanya kivuli kirudi juu hatua kumi kati ya zile kilizokuwa kimeshuka katika ngazi za Ahazi.

vi.L: Nhà tiên tri Ê-sai kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khiến bóng lùi lại trên các bậc, là các bậc nó đã đi xuống trên cầu thang của A-cha, lùi lại mười bậc.
vi.B: Bấy giờ nhà tiên tri Ê-sai kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khiến bóng nắng lùi lại mười bậc, lùi lên các bậc cầu thang của A-cha mà nó đã đi xuống.
vi.R: Bấy giờ nhà tiên tri Ê-sai kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} khiến bóng nắng lùi lên mười bậc mà nó đã đi xuống trên cầu thang của A-cha.

ko.L: 그리고 예언자 이사야가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖자, 그분께서 아하스의 계단 위로 내려갔던 그림자를 그 계단 위에서 열 계단 뒤로 물러가게 하셨다.
ko.B: 예언자 이사야가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖자, 그분께서 아하스의 계단에 내려갔던 그림자를 열 계단 뒤로 물러가게 하셨다.
ko.R: 예언자 이사야가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다. 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 아하스의 계단에서 이미 내려간 그림자를 열 계단 위로 다시 올라가게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: the steps of Ahaz: a stairway built by Ahaz, on which the moving shadow showed the time of day
decisions.reason: The word means steps or stairs. As the sun moved, a shadow crept down the stairs, marking the hours. Some take the steps as the markings of a sundial; either way the shadow moved backward, against the course of the day. Ahaz was Hezekiah's father (16:20).

decisions.choice: the LORD brought the shadow back after Isaiah called out to him
decisions.reason: Isaiah 38:8 gives God's words announcing the sign and then says "the sun went back ten steps". Kings says that Isaiah called out to the LORD and that the LORD brought the shadow back. Both speak of "the steps of Ahaz".

decisions.choice: which it had gone down: the shadow, moved by the sun
decisions.reason: The verb "had gone down" has a feminine form, which fits the word for the sun better than the word for the shadow. Isaiah 38:8 names the sun here ("gone down on the steps of Ahaz with the sun"). The sense is the same: the shadow had moved down the steps as the sun moved, and now it went back.

decisions.choice: the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the one who brought the shadow back, since a new sentence begins.

decisions.choice: "los peldaños de Acaz" (L, B); "la escalinata de Acaz" (R)
decisions.reason: The stairway on which the shadow marked the time (m1); Literal and Balanced say "peldaños", Readable names the whole stairway.

decisions.choice: naye akakirudisha (no span on the prefix)
decisions.reason: The English spans "he" (the LORD); Swahili "naye" here begins the clause and stays plain, the subject being in the verb; Readable names the LORD, as the English does.

source.text: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֡יא שָׁלַ֡ח בְּרֹאדַ֣ךְ בַּ֠לְאֲדָן בֶּֽן־בַּלְאֲדָ֧ן מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל סְפָרִ֥ים וּמִנְחָ֖ה אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י חָלָ֖ה חִזְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: At the time that sent Berodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that had been sick Hezekiah.

en.L: At that time Berodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.
en.B: About that time Berodach-baladan son of Baladan, the king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah, because he had heard that Hezekiah had been ill.
en.R: At about that time, the king of Babylon heard that Hezekiah had been sick. The king's name was Berodach-baladan son of Baladan. He sent Hezekiah letters and a gift.

es.L: En aquel tiempo Berodac-baladán hijo de Baladán, rey de Babilonia, envió cartas y un regalo a Ezequías, porque había oído que Ezequías había estado enfermo.
es.B: Por aquel tiempo Berodac-baladán hijo de Baladán, rey de Babilonia, envió cartas y un regalo a Ezequías, porque había oído que Ezequías había estado enfermo.
es.R: Por aquel tiempo el rey de Babilonia oyó que Ezequías había estado enfermo. El rey se llamaba Berodac-baladán hijo de Baladán. Le envió a Ezequías cartas y un regalo.

fr.L: En ce temps-là, Berodak-Baladân fils de Baladân, roi de Babylone, envoya des lettres et un présent à Ézéchias, car il avait appris qu’Ézéchias avait été malade.
fr.B: À cette époque, Berodak-Baladân, fils de Baladân, roi de Babylone, envoya des lettres et un présent à Ézéchias, car il avait appris qu’Ézéchias avait été malade.
fr.R: Vers cette époque, le roi de Babylone a appris qu’Ézéchias avait été malade. Ce roi s’appelait Berodak-Baladân fils de Baladân. Il a envoyé à Ézéchias des lettres et un cadeau.

sw.L: Wakati huo Berodaki-baladani mwana wa Baladani, mfalme wa Babeli, alituma barua na zawadi kwa Hezekia, kwa maana alikuwa amesikia kwamba Hezekia alikuwa ameugua.
sw.B: Karibu wakati huo Berodaki-baladani mwana wa Baladani, mfalme wa Babeli, alimtumia Hezekia barua na zawadi, kwa sababu alikuwa amesikia kwamba Hezekia alikuwa mgonjwa.
sw.R: Karibu wakati huo, mfalme wa Babeli alisikia kwamba Hezekia alikuwa mgonjwa. Jina la mfalme huyo lilikuwa Berodaki-baladani mwana wa Baladani. Akamtumia Hezekia barua na zawadi.

vi.L: Lúc ấy Bê-rô-đác Ba-la-đan con trai Ba-la-đan, vua Ba-by-lôn, gửi thư và lễ vật cho Ê-xê-chia, vì ông đã nghe rằng Ê-xê-chia bị bệnh.
vi.B: Khoảng thời gian đó, Bê-rô-đác Ba-la-đan con trai Ba-la-đan, vua Ba-by-lôn, gửi thư và quà tặng cho Ê-xê-chia, vì vua ấy nghe tin Ê-xê-chia bị bệnh.
vi.R: Khoảng thời gian đó, vua Ba-by-lôn nghe tin Ê-xê-chia bị bệnh. Vua ấy tên là Bê-rô-đác Ba-la-đan con trai Ba-la-đan. Vua ấy gửi thư và quà tặng cho Ê-xê-chia.

ko.L: 그때에 바빌론 왕 발라단의 아들 브로닥발라단이 히스기야에게 편지들과 선물을 보냈다. 히스기야가 병들었다는 소식을 들었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 무렵 바빌론 왕 발라단의 아들 브로닥발라단이 히스기야에게 편지와 선물을 보냈다. 히스기야가 병들었었다는 소식을 들었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그 무렵 바빌론 왕이 히스기야가 병들었었다는 소식을 들었다. 그 왕의 이름은 발라단의 아들 브로닥발라단이었다. 그는 히스기야에게 편지와 선물을 보냈다.

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon: Marduk-apla-iddina II, a Chaldean ruler who fought Assyria for control of Babylon
decisions.reason: He ruled Babylon from 722 to 710 BC and again briefly in 703 BC, and twice led revolts against Assyria. His embassy to Hezekiah fits that history: he was looking for allies in the west against Assyria.

decisions.choice: Berodach-baladan: the same king Isaiah 39:1 calls Merodach-baladan
decisions.reason: Kings spells the name with a B where Isaiah 39:1 has an M. Merodach is the Hebrew form of Marduk, the chief god of Babylon, so the M spelling is closer to the king's own name; the two sounds are close, and the B form may be a copying slip or another way of saying it. The record keeps the spelling each book has.

decisions.choice: a shorter reason than Isaiah 39:1
decisions.reason: Isaiah 39:1 says the king of Babylon "heard that he had been sick and had become strong". Kings says only that he had heard "that Hezekiah had been sick", and names Hezekiah again. 2 Chronicles 32:31 adds that the envoys came to ask about the sign done in the land, and that God left Hezekiah to test him.

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon heard ... He sent Hezekiah letters and a gift.
decisions.reason: Readable puts the cause first and gives the king's name in a sentence of its own, as at Isaiah 39:1.

decisions.choice: "Berodac-baladán"
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the form this verse uses; Isaiah 39:1 calls the same king Merodac-baladán (m2).

decisions.choice: Berodak-Baladân
decisions.reason: Kings spells the name with B, Isaiah 39:1 with M (m2); French keeps the spelling of each book, as the English does.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע עֲלֵיהֶם֮ חִזְקִיָּהוּ֒ וַיַּרְאֵ֣ם אֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֣ית נְכֹתֹ֡האֶת־הַכֶּסֶף֩ וְאֶת־הַזָּהָ֨ב וְאֶת־הַבְּשָׂמִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת׀שֶׁ֣מֶן הַטּ֗וֹב וְאֵת֙ בֵּ֣ית כֵּלָ֔יו וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִמְצָ֖א בְּאֽוֹצְרֹתָ֑יו לֹֽא־הָיָ֣ה דָבָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־הֶרְאָ֧ם חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּבֵית֖וֹ וּבְכָל־מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And listened to them Hezekiah, and he showed them all [the] house of his treasure, the silver and the gold and the spices and the oil the good, and [the] house of his weapons, and all that was found in his storehouses; not was a thing that not showed them Hezekiah in his house and in all his realm.

en.L: And Hezekiah listened to them, and he showed them all his treasure house, the silver and the gold and the spices and the good oil, and his armory, and all that was found in his storehouses. There was not a thing in his house and in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.
en.B: Hezekiah listened to them and showed them his whole treasury: the silver and the gold, the spices and the fine oil, his armory, and everything to be found in his storehouses. In his palace and across his whole kingdom, there was nothing he did not let them see.
en.R: Hezekiah listened to the messengers. He showed them all the silver and gold, the spices, and the expensive olive oil in his treasure house. He showed them his weapons and everything else in his storerooms. He let them see everything in his palace and in his whole kingdom.

es.L: Y Ezequías los escuchó, y les mostró toda la casa de su tesoro, la plata y el oro, y las especias y el aceite fino, y la casa de sus armas, y todo lo que se hallaba en sus almacenes. No hubo cosa en su casa ni en todo su dominio que Ezequías no les mostrara.
es.B: Ezequías los escuchó y les mostró toda la sala de su tesoro: la plata y el oro, las especias y el aceite fino, su arsenal y todo lo que había en sus almacenes. No hubo nada en su palacio ni en todo su reino que no les dejara ver.
es.R: Ezequías escuchó a los mensajeros. Les mostró toda la plata y el oro, las especias y el aceite de oliva fino que tenía en la sala del tesoro. Les mostró sus armas y todo lo demás que había en sus almacenes. Les dejó ver todo lo que había en su palacio y en todo su reino.

fr.L: Et Ézéchias les écouta, et il leur montra toute sa maison du trésor, l’argent et l’or, et les aromates et l’huile fine, et sa maison des armes, et tout ce qui se trouvait dans ses magasins ; il n’y eut rien qu’Ézéchias ne leur montrât dans sa maison et dans tout son domaine.
fr.B: Ézéchias écouta les envoyés et leur fit voir toute sa salle du trésor : l’argent et l’or, les aromates et l’huile fine, son arsenal, et tout ce qui se trouvait dans ses magasins. Dans son palais et dans tout son royaume, il n’y eut rien qu’il ne leur montrât.
fr.R: Ézéchias a écouté les messagers. Il leur a montré tout l’argent et l’or, les aromates et l’huile d’olive précieuse de sa salle du trésor. Il leur a montré ses armes et tout ce qu’il y avait dans ses réserves. Il leur a fait voir tout ce qu’il y avait dans son palais et dans tout son royaume.

sw.L: Naye Hezekia akawasikiliza, akawaonyesha nyumba yote ya hazina yake, fedha na dhahabu na manukato na mafuta mazuri, na nyumba ya silaha zake, na vyote vilivyoonekana katika ghala zake. Hakuna kitu katika nyumba yake na katika milki yake yote ambacho Hezekia hakuwaonyesha.
sw.B: Hezekia aliwasikiliza, akawaonyesha nyumba yake yote ya hazina: fedha na dhahabu, manukato na mafuta mazuri, ghala lake la silaha, na kila kitu kilichokuwa katika ghala zake. Katika ikulu yake na katika ufalme wake wote hakukuwa na kitu ambacho hakuwaonyesha.
sw.R: Hezekia aliwasikiliza wajumbe hao. Akawaonyesha fedha yote na dhahabu, manukato, na mafuta ya zeituni ya bei ghali yaliyokuwa katika nyumba yake ya hazina. Akawaonyesha silaha zake na kila kitu kingine kilichokuwa katika ghala zake. Aliwaacha waone kila kitu katika jumba lake na katika ufalme wake wote.

vi.L: Ê-xê-chia nghe họ, và cho họ xem cả kho báu của mình: bạc, vàng, hương liệu và dầu quý, kho vũ khí của mình, và mọi thứ có trong các kho của mình. Không có vật gì trong cung và trong khắp lãnh thổ của mình mà Ê-xê-chia không cho họ xem.
vi.B: Ê-xê-chia tiếp đón họ và cho họ xem toàn bộ kho báu của mình: bạc và vàng, hương liệu và dầu quý, kho vũ khí, và mọi thứ có trong các kho của vua. Trong cung điện và khắp vương quốc, không có gì vua không cho họ xem.
vi.R: Ê-xê-chia tiếp các sứ giả. Vua cho họ xem tất cả bạc vàng, hương liệu và dầu ô-liu đắt tiền trong kho báu của mình. Vua cho họ xem các vũ khí và mọi thứ khác trong các kho. Vua cho họ xem mọi thứ trong cung điện và trong khắp vương quốc.

ko.L: 그리고 히스기야가 그들의 말을 듣고, 그들에게 그의 보물 창고 전체, 곧 은과 금과 향료와 좋은 기름과 그의 무기고와 그의 창고들에 있는 모든 것을 보여 주었다. 히스기야가 그의 왕궁과 그의 온 나라에서 그들에게 보여 주지 않은 것이 하나도 없었다.
ko.B: 히스기야는 그들을 반갑게 맞아들이고, 보물 창고 전체, 곧 은과 금과 향료와 귀한 기름과 무기고와 창고에 있는 모든 것을 보여 주었다. 그의 왕궁과 온 나라에서 그가 그들에게 보여 주지 않은 것이 하나도 없었다.
ko.R: 히스기야는 사자들의 말을 들어 주었다. 그는 보물 창고에 있는 은과 금과 향료와 비싼 올리브기름을 모두 그들에게 보여 주었다. 무기들과 창고에 있는 다른 모든 것도 보여 주었다. 그는 왕궁과 온 나라에 있는 것을 하나도 빠짐없이 그들에게 보여 주었다.

decisions.choice: listened to them: gave the envoys a hearing
decisions.reason: Isaiah 39:2 has a verb that differs by one letter in Hebrew: Hezekiah "rejoiced over them". Kings has "listened to them", that is, he heard their message with favor. Both readings show a king pleased to be courted by a foreign power.

decisions.choice: his treasure house and his armory: the wealth and the military strength of the kingdom
decisions.reason: Showing a foreign envoy one's treasure and weapons was a way of proving one's worth as an ally. The treasury had been emptied to pay Sennacherib (18:15-16), so this display may belong to the years after the Assyrian crisis or be part of it; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: the good oil: fine olive oil, a costly product kept in royal stores
decisions.reason: Fine oil was a valued trade good and was stored with spices and precious metals (2 Chronicles 32:27-28).

decisions.choice: otherwise the same as Isaiah 39:2, with "all" in a different place
decisions.reason: Kings says Hezekiah showed them "all his treasure house" and "his armory"; Isaiah 39:2 has "his treasure house" and "all his armory". The rest of the verse is the same and is rendered the same way.

decisions.choice: palace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the king's house; Literal keeps "house".

records.literal_gloss: And came Isaiah the prophet to the king Hezekiah and said to him, what did they say the men these, and from where do they come to you? And said Hezekiah, from a land distant they have come, from Babylon.

en.L: And Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say, and from where do they come to you?" And Hezekiah said, "From a distant land they have come, from Babylon."
en.B: Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and asked him, "What did these men say? And where did they come from to visit you?" Hezekiah answered, "They came from a faraway country, from Babylon."
en.R: Then the prophet Isaiah went to King Hezekiah. He asked, "What did these men say? Where did they come from?" Hezekiah answered, "They came from a country far away. They came from Babylon."

es.L: Y el profeta Isaías vino al rey Ezequías y le dijo: «¿Qué dijeron estos hombres, y de dónde vienen a ti?». Y Ezequías dijo: «De una tierra lejana han venido, de Babilonia».
es.B: Entonces el profeta Isaías fue a ver al rey Ezequías y le preguntó: «¿Qué dijeron estos hombres? ¿Y de dónde vinieron a visitarte?». Ezequías le respondió: «Vinieron de un país lejano, de Babilonia».
es.R: Entonces el profeta Isaías fue a ver al rey Ezequías. Le preguntó: «¿Qué dijeron estos hombres? ¿De dónde vinieron?». Ezequías le respondió: «Vinieron de un país lejano. Vinieron de Babilonia».

fr.L: Et Isaïe le prophète vint auprès du roi Ézéchias et lui dit : « Qu’ont dit ces hommes, et d’où viennent-ils vers toi ? » Et Ézéchias dit : « D’un pays lointain ils sont venus, de Babylone. »
fr.B: Alors le prophète Isaïe vint trouver le roi Ézéchias et lui demanda : « Qu’ont dit ces hommes ? D’où sont-ils venus te voir ? » Ézéchias répondit : « Ils sont venus d’un pays lointain, de Babylone. »
fr.R: Alors le prophète Isaïe est allé voir le roi Ézéchias. Il lui a demandé : « Qu’ont dit ces hommes ? D’où venaient-ils ? » Ézéchias a répondu : « Ils venaient d’un pays très loin d’ici. Ils venaient de Babylone. »

sw.L: Naye Isaya nabii akaja kwa mfalme Hezekia, akamwambia, "Watu hawa walisema nini, na wametoka wapi kuja kwako?" Naye Hezekia akasema, "Wametoka nchi ya mbali, kutoka Babeli."
sw.B: Kisha nabii Isaya alikuja kwa mfalme Hezekia, akamwuliza, "Watu hawa walisema nini? Na wametoka wapi kuja kukutembelea?" Hezekia akajibu, "Walitoka nchi ya mbali, kutoka Babeli."
sw.R: Kisha nabii Isaya alikwenda kwa mfalme Hezekia. Akamwuliza, "Watu hawa walisema nini? Walitoka wapi?" Hezekia akajibu, "Walitoka nchi ya mbali. Walitoka Babeli."

vi.L: Nhà tiên tri Ê-sai đến cùng vua Ê-xê-chia và nói với vua: "Những người ấy đã nói gì, và họ từ đâu đến với vua?" Ê-xê-chia đáp: "Họ đến từ một xứ xa, từ Ba-by-lôn."
vi.B: Bấy giờ nhà tiên tri Ê-sai đến gặp vua Ê-xê-chia và hỏi: "Những người ấy đã nói gì? Họ từ đâu đến thăm vua?" Ê-xê-chia đáp: "Họ đến từ một xứ xa, từ Ba-by-lôn."
vi.R: Bấy giờ nhà tiên tri Ê-sai đến gặp vua Ê-xê-chia. Ông hỏi: "Những người ấy đã nói gì? Họ từ đâu đến?" Ê-xê-chia đáp: "Họ đến từ một xứ ở rất xa. Họ đến từ Ba-by-lôn."

ko.L: 그리고 예언자 이사야가 히스기야 왕에게 와서 그에게 말했다. "이 사람들이 무슨 말을 했습니까? 그리고 그들이 어디에서 임금님께 왔습니까?" 히스기야가 말했다. "그들은 먼 땅, 바빌론에서 왔소."
ko.B: 그때 예언자 이사야가 히스기야 왕에게 와서 물었다. "이 사람들이 무슨 말을 했습니까? 그들이 어디에서 임금님을 찾아왔습니까?" 히스기야가 대답했다. "먼 나라, 바빌론에서 왔소."
ko.R: 그러자 예언자 이사야가 히스기야 왕에게 가서 물었다. "이 사람들이 무슨 말을 했습니까? 그들은 어디에서 왔습니까?" 히스기야가 대답했다. "먼 나라에서 왔소. 바빌론에서 왔소."

decisions.choice: a distant land: Babylon, far to the east beyond the desert
decisions.reason: Hezekiah answers only the second question and says nothing of what the envoys said. The phrase "from a distant land" echoes what the Gibeonites claimed in Joshua 9:6-9 when they sought a treaty with Israel.

decisions.choice: the same as Isaiah 39:3 except "to me"
decisions.reason: Isaiah 39:3 has Hezekiah say "they have come to me"; Kings has "they have come". Otherwise the verse is the same and is rendered the same way.

records.literal_gloss: And he said, what did they see in your house? And said Hezekiah, all that [is] in my house they saw; not was a thing that not I showed them in my storehouses.

en.L: And he said, "What did they see in your house?" And Hezekiah said, "All that [is] in my house they saw; there was not a thing in my storehouses that I did not show them."
en.B: He asked, "What did they see in your palace?" Hezekiah replied, "They saw all that is in my palace. In my storerooms there is not a thing I failed to show them."
en.R: Isaiah asked, "What did they see in your palace?" Hezekiah said, "They saw everything in my palace. I showed them everything in my storerooms."

es.L: Y dijo: «¿Qué vieron en tu casa?». Y Ezequías dijo: «Todo lo que [hay] en mi casa vieron; no hubo cosa en mis almacenes que no les mostrara».
es.B: Isaías preguntó: «¿Qué vieron en tu palacio?». Ezequías respondió: «Vieron todo lo que hay en mi palacio. No hay nada en mis almacenes que no les haya mostrado».
es.R: Isaías le preguntó: «¿Qué vieron en tu palacio?». Ezequías le dijo: «Vieron todo lo que hay en mi palacio. Les mostré todo lo que hay en mis almacenes».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Qu’ont-ils vu dans ta maison ? » Et Ézéchias dit : « Tout ce qui [est] dans ma maison, ils l’ont vu ; il n’y a rien dans mes magasins que je ne leur aie montré. »
fr.B: Isaïe demanda : « Qu’ont-ils vu dans ton palais ? » Ézéchias répondit : « Ils ont vu tout ce qu’il y a dans mon palais. Il n’y a rien dans mes réserves que je ne leur aie montré. »
fr.R: Isaïe a demandé : « Qu’ont-ils vu dans ton palais ? » Ézéchias a répondu : « Ils ont vu tout ce qu’il y a dans mon palais. Je leur ai montré tout ce qu’il y a dans mes réserves. »

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Waliona nini katika nyumba yako?" Naye Hezekia akasema, "Waliona vyote vilivyomo katika nyumba yangu; hakuna kitu katika ghala zangu ambacho sikuwaonyesha."
sw.B: Akauliza, "Waliona nini katika ikulu yako?" Hezekia akajibu, "Waliona vyote vilivyomo katika ikulu yangu. Hakuna kitu katika ghala zangu ambacho sikuwaonyesha."
sw.R: Isaya akauliza, "Waliona nini katika jumba lako?" Hezekia akasema, "Waliona kila kitu katika jumba langu. Niliwaonyesha kila kitu kilichomo katika ghala zangu."

vi.B: Ê-sai hỏi: "Họ đã thấy gì trong cung điện của vua?" Ê-xê-chia đáp: "Họ đã thấy mọi thứ trong cung điện ta. Trong các kho của ta, không có vật gì ta không cho họ xem."
vi.R: Ê-sai hỏi: "Họ đã thấy gì trong cung điện của vua?" Ê-xê-chia đáp: "Họ đã thấy mọi thứ trong cung điện ta. Ta đã cho họ xem mọi thứ trong các kho của ta."

ko.L: 그리고 그가 말했다. "그들이 임금님의 집에서 무엇을 보았습니까?" 히스기야가 말했다. "내 집에 있는 모든 것을 그들이 보았소. 내 창고들에 있는 것 가운데 내가 그들에게 보여 주지 않은 것이 하나도 없소."

ko.R: 이사야가 물었다. "그들이 왕궁에서 무엇을 보았습니까?" 히스기야가 대답했다. "그들은 내 왕궁에 있는 모든 것을 보았소. 나는 내 창고에 있는 것을 다 보여 주었소."

decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse is the same as Isaiah 39:4, and it is rendered the same way.

decisions.reason: Isaiah 39:5 has "the word of the LORD of hosts". Kings has the shorter "the word of the LORD". Otherwise the verse is the same as Isaiah 39:5 and is rendered the same way.

records.literal_gloss: Look, days [are] coming, and will be carried off all that [is] in your house and that have stored up your fathers until the day this, to Babylon; not will be left a thing, says Yahweh.

en.L: Look, days are coming when all that [is] in your house, and that your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon; not a thing will be left, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Look, a time is coming when all that is in your palace, everything your ancestors have laid up until today, will be hauled off to Babylon. Not one thing will remain, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Someday everything in your palace will be taken away to Babylon. All the treasures your ancestors saved up until now will be taken. Nothing will be left. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says.

es.L: He aquí que vienen días en que todo lo que [hay] en tu casa, y lo que tus padres han atesorado hasta este día, será llevado a Babilonia; no quedará nada, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Mira, se acerca el tiempo en que todo lo que hay en tu palacio, todo lo que tus antepasados han guardado hasta hoy, será llevado a Babilonia. No quedará nada, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Algún día todo lo que hay en tu palacio será llevado a Babilonia. Se llevarán todos los tesoros que tus antepasados guardaron hasta ahora. No quedará nada. Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Voici, des jours viennent où tout ce qui [est] dans ta maison, et ce que tes pères ont amassé jusqu’à ce jour, sera emporté à Babylone ; il n’en restera rien, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Le temps vient où tout ce qui est dans ton palais, tout ce que tes ancêtres ont amassé jusqu’à aujourd’hui, sera emporté à Babylone. Il n’en restera rien, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Un jour, tout ce qu’il y a dans ton palais sera emporté à Babylone. Tous les trésors que tes ancêtres ont mis de côté jusqu’à aujourd’hui seront emportés. Il ne restera rien. C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui le dit.

sw.L: Tazama, siku zinakuja ambapo vyote vilivyomo katika nyumba yako, na vile walivyoweka akiba baba zako mpaka siku hii, vitachukuliwa mpaka Babeli; hakitabaki kitu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Tazama, wakati unakuja ambapo vyote vilivyomo katika ikulu yako, kila kitu ambacho babu zako wameweka akiba mpaka leo, vitachukuliwa mpaka Babeli. Hakitabaki hata kitu kimoja, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Siku moja kila kitu kilichomo katika jumba lako kitachukuliwa mpaka Babeli. Hazina zote ambazo babu zako walikusanya mpaka sasa zitachukuliwa. Hakuna kitakachobaki. Hivyo ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anavyosema.

vi.L: Này, những ngày đang đến, khi mọi thứ trong cung vua, và những gì tổ phụ vua đã tích trữ cho đến ngày nay, sẽ bị chở đi Ba-by-lôn; không còn sót lại vật gì, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Này, sẽ đến lúc mọi thứ trong cung điện vua, tất cả những gì tổ tiên vua đã tích trữ cho đến ngày nay, sẽ bị chở sang Ba-by-lôn. Sẽ không còn sót lại gì cả, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Một ngày kia mọi thứ trong cung điện vua sẽ bị đem sang Ba-by-lôn. Tất cả của cải tổ tiên vua đã cất giữ cho đến nay sẽ bị lấy đi. Sẽ không còn lại gì cả. Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: '보아라, 날들이 오고 있다. 네 집에 있는 모든 것과 네 조상들이 오늘까지 쌓아 둔 것이 바빌론으로 옮겨질 것이다. 하나도 남지 않을 것이다.' {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하십니다.
ko.B: '보아라, 때가 오고 있다. 그때에 네 왕궁에 있는 모든 것과 네 조상들이 오늘까지 쌓아 둔 모든 것이 바빌론으로 실려 갈 것이다. 하나도 남지 않을 것이다.' {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하십니다.
ko.R: '언젠가 네 왕궁에 있는 모든 것이 바빌론으로 실려 갈 것이다. 네 조상들이 지금까지 모아 둔 보물들이 모두 실려 갈 것이다. 아무것도 남지 않을 것이다.' 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀입니다.

decisions.choice: carried off to Babylon: the first word in Kings of exile to Babylon
decisions.reason: At this time Babylon was a small power looking to Judah for help against Assyria. The word looks ahead more than a century to Nebuchadnezzar, who carried off the treasures of the temple and the palace (24:13; 25:13-15).

decisions.choice: your fathers: your ancestors, the earlier kings of Judah
decisions.reason: The treasures had been stored up by the kings before Hezekiah. "Until this day" here is Hezekiah's own day, the time Isaiah is speaking.

decisions.choice: word for word the same as Isaiah 39:6
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse is the same as Isaiah 39:6, and it is rendered the same way.

en.B: Some of your descendants, born of your own line, will be taken away, and they will serve as eunuchs in the palace of the Babylonian king."
en.R: Some of your own descendants will be taken away. They will be made eunuchs and will serve in the palace of the king of Babylon."

sw.R: Baadhi ya wazao wako mwenyewe watachukuliwa. Watahasiwa na kufanywa matowashi, nao watatumika katika jumba la mfalme wa Babeli."

vi.B: Một số con cháu của vua, là dòng dõi ruột thịt của vua, sẽ bị bắt đi, và họ sẽ làm hoạn quan trong cung điện của vua Ba-by-lôn."
vi.R: Một số con cháu của chính vua sẽ bị bắt đi. Họ sẽ bị biến thành hoạn quan và phải phục vụ trong cung điện của vua Ba-by-lôn."

ko.L: '그리고 네게서 나올 네 아들들, 네가 낳을 자들 가운데 몇을 그들이 데려갈 것이고, 그들은 바빌론 왕의 궁전에서 내시가 될 것이다.'"
ko.B: '네 몸에서 태어날 네 자손 가운데 몇이 끌려가서 바빌론 왕의 궁전에서 내시가 될 것이다.'"
ko.R: '네 자손 가운데 몇이 끌려갈 것이다. 그들은 내시가 되어 바빌론 왕의 궁전에서 일하게 될 것이다.'"

decisions.choice: your sons: your descendants, the royal family after you
decisions.reason: Sons often means descendants. The words "who will come from you, whom you will father" stress that it will be Hezekiah's own line. Daniel 1:3 tells of young men of the royal family taken to serve in the palace of Babylon.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: castrated servants at a foreign court
decisions.reason: The word can mean any high court official (it is used of Potiphar, a married man, in Genesis 39:1), but in a foreign king's palace, of captives taken from a royal family, it most likely means eunuchs, as at Isaiah 39:7 and 56:3-4.

decisions.choice: they will take: the reading given in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text give "he will take"; the Hebrew margin reads "they will take", as Isaiah 39:7 has in its text. Either way the sense is that they will be taken away; the margin's reading is followed. Apart from this the verse is the same as Isaiah 39:7 and is rendered the same way.

decisions.choice: will be made eunuchs and will serve
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what being eunuchs in the palace means.

decisions.choice: eunuchs
decisions.reason: These books usually say "officials" for this word at Balanced and Readable. Here every level keeps "eunuchs", as Isaiah 39:7 does, because the sense is most likely the literal one (m2).

decisions.choice: "eunucos" at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note sets "eunucos" at Literal and "funcionarios" at Balanced and Readable; here, as the English does, every level keeps "eunucos", since the threat is that the king's sons will be made eunuchs.

decisions.choice: "eunuques" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the word means castrated servants at a foreign court (m2), so French keeps "eunuques" at every level, as the English does, instead of the "hauts fonctionnaires" the terms note sets where *sarisim* means officials.

decisions.choice: matowashi at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note has "matowashi" (Literal) and "maafisa" (Balanced, Readable) for this word; here the English keeps "eunuchs" at every level, since the shame of the prophecy lies in it, and Swahili does the same.

decisions.choice: hoạn quan at every level
decisions.reason: The word is "triều thần" and "quan chức" at Balanced and Readable elsewhere in these books, but here, as in the English, every level says "hoạn quan": the threat is that the king's line will be made eunuchs.

decisions.choice: "내시" at every level here
alternatives: "관리" (B, R), as the terms note gives for *sarisim*
decisions.reason: The English keeps "eunuchs" at every level in this verse because the shame of it is the point of the prophecy; Korean follows, though elsewhere the word is "관리" at Balanced and Readable.
